sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Code civil, Code de commerce; regulatory overlay of EU directives)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD and Council of Europe, amended 2011)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) provisions on freedom of establishment and cross-border e-commerce

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-45 and L. 561-46 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF) and Articles R. 561-52 to R. 561-57 of the CMF; Loi No. 2012-352 of 12 March 2012; Ordonnance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD); Ordonnance No. 2020-1635 of 21 December 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); décret No. 2021-1427 relative to the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access restricted to legitimate-interest requesters under Article L. 561-47-1 of the CMF)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each shareholder, beneficial owner and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorised notary, civil registry, or competent consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate register extract of any foreign corporate shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or trade register in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague members, French consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (statuts) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notaire or French corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed if executed in France; Hague Apostille if executed outside a Hague member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank attestation of payment or blocking of share capital (attestation de blocage de fonds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: ACPR-authorised credit institution in France or in the currency-hosting jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for foreign institutions; simple bank letter for authorised French institutions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office domiciliation (lease or domiciliation agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) or property owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for original foreign lease agreements; otherwise notarized attestation by French domiciliation company

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, beneficial owners, managers and authorized signatories against the French Ministry of Economy's territorial freeze list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions transposed by EU regulation, and the US OFAC SDN list where STRIPE or PAYPAL processing in USD is planned. Politically exposed persons must be identified through self-certification and cross-checked against licensed commercial PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required where a PEP, a high-risk source of funds, or a link to a sanctioned country is identified. TRACFIN reporting obligations and Article L. 561-15 CMF apply; the SARL shall maintain written AML procedures and appoint a designated AML/KYC compliance officer before the opening of any French or cross-border banking account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (GUF), operated by Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; cross-check against Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official filing language of the RCS is French. The corporate name may contain expressions in any language, but for inclusion in the RCS it must be written in Latin script with the appropriate French diacritics. A non-Latin script name (e.g., Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters, and that transliterated version becomes the statutory registered name. The legal-form suffix 'S.A.R.L.' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' must appear immediately after the corporate name on official documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a statutory pre-incorporation name-reservation window. A proposed SARL name is cleared only at the time of article-of-association filing and RCS registration through the Guichet Unique. If the registrar rejects the name as misleading, contrary to public order, or conflicting with an existing RCS name or third-party trademarks, the applicant may (i) revise and resubmit the application immediately through the Guichet Unique; and (ii) file a written petition within 15 days from receipt of the refusal with the judge responsible for supervising the company registry (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) under Article L. 123-5-2 of the Code de commerce. An expedited appeal may be brought before the first president of the relevant Cour d'appel within a further 15-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a SARL in the online fashion watch and jewelry e-commerce industry. A commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) may provide the registered French address under Articles L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-33 to R. 123-36 of the Code de commerce, for a maximum period of five years from formation. After that period, physical premises must be established. The virtual office is accepted as the SIRET/registered-office address, provided that the address is contactable during business hours, registered with the CCI/Greffe, and that all statutory accounting records and UBO files can be physically accessed by DGFiP, URSSAF, and the commercial court if inspected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. For a registered office at a commercial domiciliation company, the annualized probability of an unannounced physical or documentary inspection is approximately 10%. If a home-based or private virtual address is declared, this probability increases to approximately 20% in the first year. The inspection is primarily documentary—verification of the Kbis, UBO declaration, physical access to the registered address, and the availability of the manager or legal agent—rather than a warehouse or inventory audit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and trademark pre-clearance search in RCS, Infogreffe, and INPI databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI / Infogreffe data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public tariff plus service provider search fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French-law Articles of Association (statuts) and legal review of SARL incorporation structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate lawyer or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal fee at prevailing French market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation, notarization, translation, and apostille of foreign corporate documents and UBO identification file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille office / French consulate / certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee plus notarial and translation tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing through Guichet Unique and UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
Publication of the incorporation notice in an approved legal-announcement journal (journal d'annonces légales)
Registered-office virtual domiciliation service for the first 12 months
AML/KYC screening subscription for PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media checks on all UBOS and managers
Bank account opening support and capital-blocking attestation (attestation de blocage de fonds)
Notary fee for certification of capital payment, where required by the banking partner or domiciliation agreement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL), and Articles R. 223-1 to R. 223-27 (registration procedure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry Clerk) via the Guichet Unique administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la Société (Articles of Association) and Form M0 (Demande d'immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL; capital is freely determined in the articles. Cash contributions must be subscribed in full, and at least 20% of each cash share must be paid up at incorporation (Article L. 223-7 C.com), with the balance payable within 5 years. No escrow account is required if capital is imposed; funds may be deposited with a bank or notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders hereby adopt the draft Articles of Association for the limited liability company (SARL) and approve the subscription of shares as recorded in the capital subscription list; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be fixed at the address specified in the Articles and all statutory formalities shall be carried out from that address; RESOLVED, that each shareholder shall pay, to the entity's bank account or the societe d'avocats, at least 20% of the subscribed cash contributions prior to registration; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial manager (Gérant) appointed in the Articles is hereby confirmed to take office with full powers to represent the company and to accomplish all incorporation filings; RESOLVED, that the manager is authorized to sign the registration form, publish the legal notice, and complete the RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / Infogreffe (national database), assisted by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search on Infogreffe against existing trademarks and company names. Optionally file an ‘INPI’ trademark application for the brand name (€190 by e-filing). Obtain a negative certificate of search or a reservation receipt; the reserved name must be used within 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing trademark, submit a new name with added distinctive element (e.g., geographic suffix) and re-file; file opposition response before the INPI within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Articles of Association and appointment of manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary if real property contribution, otherwise by private deed before the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French, specifying share capital, share distribution, manager powers, registered office, and corporate object limited to online merchandising of jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories. All founders must sign the drafted articles (either in wet ink or via electronic signature compliant with eIDAS). Attach a report of the legal representative if the manager is appointed in a separate act.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts signed by all shareholders
Declaration of subscription and payment of shares
Power of attorney (if signatories are represented)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry observes inconsistencies, correct the statuts and obtain a fresh signature of all shareholders within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Evidence of capital deposit and contribution verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank or notary authorized to receive funds on behalf of the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company bank account (or notary escrow) and deposit cash contributions, receiving a certificate of deposit from the banker or notary. For contributions in kind, obtain a contribution report from the commissaire aux apports if the value exceeds 30,000 euros or if not representable by an expert. The deposit certificate must state that the amount is blocked until RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Blocked funds certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds)
Bank account opening form or notary escrow agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank rejects the certificate due to naming inconsistency, correct the spelling of the company name in bank records and ask the bank to re-issue the attestation within the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a legal notice in a journal of legal announcements (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcements journal in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause a notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) to be published in an approved legal publication, mentioning the corporate name, SARL designation, capital amount, registered office, corporate object, duration (99 years), and manager identity. Obtain the JAL attestation of publication.
required_dossiers: Payment of publication fee (approx. EUR 90-200 depending on journal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice due to incorrect content, submit a corrected notice and republish; pay an additional publication fee only if the correction materially changes the published text.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier via the Guichet Unique and obtain RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique (INPI) – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the digital M0 form on the Guichet Unique portal, upload the signed statuts, proof of registered office, evidence of capital deposit, JAL publication attestation, and the manager’s identity documents. Pay the court clerk fee (approx. EUR 78.48). The RCS registrar verifies and issues an immatriculation certificate (extrait K-bis) with SIREN/SIRET numbers and an activity code (APE).
required_dossiers: Articles of Association (notarized or private deed)
Proof of address for the registered office (lease, deed, or utility bill)
Identity and nationality documents of the manager
Declaration of non-conviction for the manager
Proof of effective office use (if managed address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a query, the applicant receives a notification via Guichet Unique; respond with the requested corrections within 15 days. Re-submit the M0 form and corrected annexes; the registration may be refused if the company object includes unauthorized activities, in which case amend the object and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration social, employment, and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF / INSEE / Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the K-bis, validate the creation of the business with URSSAF (social security registration occurs automatically after RCS, but confirm the employer number), complete the income tax declaration (form 1423-SD) with the local tax office, and order the training of VAT number from the DGFiP. Keep the K-bis as official proof and display the VAT number on invoices.
required_dossiers: Identity of the manager (for liability matters)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF delays, apply for a mandatory registration acknowledgement by email and attach the K-bis extract; if necessary, obtain an interlocuteur unique from URSSAF via the online chat.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Sous-préfecture / Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DREETS) – specifically the Unité de Contrôle des Installations Classées
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A – Exempt from industrial operating license (no manufacturing, assembly, or finishing operations). The activity is a pure e-commerce retail and distribution of jewelry and watches.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – Registered Office: Département des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration under the 'rubrique 2615' (Non-hazardous waste) may apply only for storage of up to 1,000 kg of commercial waste; no formal EIA is required for an online retail activity. The entity is classified under the 'no notice' / 'exempt from full EIA' category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For wastewater discharge from office premises, compliance with municipal sanitation regulations (max 15m³/day for surface runoff); VOCs from packaging adhesives must remain below 0.5 g/L active solvent; waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) from returned watches with batteries must be separately collected and recycled via an approved eco-organism (e.g., Ecosystem or Ecologic). General waste storage shall not exceed 50 kg of hazardous residues per quarter without a specific waste exemption.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Commission de Sécurité (SDIS) may be required only if office premises are open to public (e.g., showroom), but for pure online office e-commerce, the workplace must obtain an attestation of conformity from the occupational health service (SMVT) confirming fire exits, emergency lighting, and first aid equipment. Structural load inspection is not required for standard office, but the registered office must include a workplace licence (autorisation d’exploitation) under the urban planning code (Code de l'urbanisme) if the commercial activity alters the premises’ use. Covid/occupational clearance is replaced by the general risk assessment (Document Unique) filed with the CSE. The manager must ensure workers receive basic first aid training and establish a workplace inspection register.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) / Online portal: impots.gouv.fr (business portal: www.impots.gouv.fr/accueil; e-invoicing platform: Chorus Pro)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity making taxable supplies in France must register with DGFiP for French value-added tax (TVA). Obtain a French SIREN/SIRET number from the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) if the entity has a permanent establishment; otherwise, register direct for a French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) using the pre-registration portal of the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects or the EU VAT registration procedure.  The application must identify the fiscal representative in France if no permanent establishment and the entity is outside the EU. Required documentation: certificate of incorporation, proof of EU/TIN registration, description of the business activity, and expected French taxable turnover. The French VAT number is normally issued within 2–6 weeks. For domestic SARLs, the TIN is the SIRET number and the VAT number is obtained automatically upon registration at the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS), qualifying as an entity-level taxpayer. A new SARL may elect, for a maximum period of five fiscal years, to be taxed as a partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) under Article 239 bis A of the French General Tax Code. Subsequent irrevocable option for IS is possible. France also permits tax consolidation (régime de l'intégration fiscale) for groups holding at least 95% of the subsidiary. No 'check-the-box' election comparable to the US exists; hybrid mismatch rules under European Directive ATAD are implemented, including reverse hybrid classification rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General domestic VAT registration is required without threshold for foreign entities selling goods in France via e-commerce. For intra-Community distance sales of goods by EU-established suppliers, the applicable French distance-selling threshold is EUR 10,000 (annual aggregate across all EU supplies, triggering French registration if exceeded). A French-established small enterprise may benefit from the 'franchise en base' exemption for sales of goods up to EUR 91,900 (2025), reducing the need to charge VAT below that level; this exemption is not available to foreign-established entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing for all transactions between taxable persons established in France, with a phased implementation from 1 September 2026 (all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices; issuance obligation begins 1 September 2026 for large/medium, 1 September 2027 for small). Invoices must be transmitted as structured electronic documents (Factur-X, PEPPOL, etc.) to the Chorus Pro platform for clearance against the DGFiP. E-reporting of transaction data is required for B2B and B2C cross-border supplies and payment transactions. Real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping are not required for all retail e-commerce; however, online marketplaces must report seller turnover and payments. Since 2023, France has required payment service providers to transmit electronic payment data to the Tax Administration for all cross-border and domestic retail sales, enabling indirect tax monitoring.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods to a destination outside the European Union qualifies for French VAT at 0% if the export is substantiated by proof of removal from the EU within the statutory timeframe (generally 90 days from invoice; exports of goods supplied from France to non-EU customers in the normal course of trade are zero-rated absolutely). Transfer of goods to an EU member state that triggers intra-Community supply is generally exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, not zero-rated, but may be zero-rated under certain conditions. Services directly linked to exported goods (e.g., freight, insurance, loading) may be zero-rated. The customer must be outside France/EU and the goods must physically leave French customs territory; the VAT exemption is denied where the evidence does not establish a genuine external transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU – Document Administratif Unique)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (International Consignment Note)
Supplier's Export Evidence (Broker's export certificate, customs manifest)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Proof of Receipt of payment from the non-EU counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to retrospective audit by DGFiP. Where documentary evidence is false, incomplete, or where goods re-enter the EU or were diverted, the tax authority reassesses VAT at the standard or reduced rate, imposes a 100% fine of the evaded tax (Article 1729 CGI), plus 80% restitution interest, and may apply a 40% penalty for deliberate negligence. Criminal penalties may apply for customs declaration fraud. The foreign exchange repatriation obligation is enforced by customs law (monetary obligations) with non-compliance penalties up to 50% of the unrepatriated sum. Claims for refund of French VAT on export-related input taxes require strict compliance with Articles 271 and 242-0 L of the French tax code and may be rejected upon incomplete documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank); foreign exchange and financial surveillance co-supervised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (DGT) of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. France applies full free movement of capital under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions; no exchange control authorization is required for EUR-denominated or cross-border payments. Profit remittance is free of exchange restrictions; the only impositions are corporate income tax on French-source profits (25% standard rate, 15% reduced rate for SMEs below thresholds) and dividend withholding tax (25% standard domestic rate, reduced by tax treaties, fully exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 2 years). Repatriation of trade proceeds faces no Bank of France surrender or licensing hurdle; bank statements and MT103 records must be preserved for ACPR/Tracfin inspection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio applies in France; exporters may hold export proceeds in foreign currency in authorized banks. Balance-of-payments statistical declarations to Banque de France are required for individual cross-border capital transactions (loan, equity, real estate) exceeding EUR 15 million; trade-related payments for goods and ordinary services remain below the reporting threshold and need no declaration. All wire transfers must carry complete remitter and beneficiary information under EU Regulation 2015/847 to support AML screening.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Professionnel) and Capital Escrow Account (Compte de Dépôt de Capital)
Operational Account (Compte Pro) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (Compte Professionnel) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (Compte Professionnel) – limited suitability for high-value goods treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility with strict legal constraints. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Treezor, and EU-passported EMIs (e.g., SWIIP, Checkout.com) may open French IBANs for the SARL; they provide faster onboarding and are PSD2-compliant. Constraints include: (1) safeguarding of funds rather than bank deposit guarantee, (2) limited credit and FX-Hedging product availability, (3) mandatory ACPR authorization or European passport notification, and (4) e-money accounts cannot be used to benefit from the droit au compte guarantee of Banque de France. Offshore and non-EEA EMIs (e.g., UK-only FCA or US-chartered) have Low feasibility for primary treasury use; they may be used only as secondary collections channels after ACPR cross-border services authorization review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory at tier-1 French banks for a SARL with a non-resident gérant. The French Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L561-5 to L561-7 CMF) and ACPR typology impose an in-person meeting with the relationship manager or a certified videoconference under ACPR digital onboarding rules; market practice at BNPP, SG and CACF still requires the gérant and beneficial owners to appear in branch at least once. Remote onboarding is accepted only by certain EMIs and online affiliates. Original documents or notarized copies: passport, Kbis extract, statuts, RBE beneficial ownership declaration, resolution appointing the gérant, proof of registered office, and 3 months of bank statements (where applicable).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or gérant resident in a non-EU, high-risk or tax-favored jurisdiction; the bank classifies the file as high-risk PEP or high-money-laundering-risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of Funds Declaration (cerfa form), 12-month audited or bank-certified personal account statements, tax residence certificate (e.g., US IRS Form 6166, UK HMRC), corporate registry extract with chain of ownership, notarized identity documents, evidence of business substance (lease, employees), and a written explanation of the transaction chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: online jewelry, watches and fashion classified as 'high-value goods' under Article 1.2° of the French anti-money-laundering order (high turnover small items, cross-border shipping).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registration (SIREN/SIRET), statuts, ISIC 4791 activity declaration, supply-chain invoices from authorized distributors, brand authorization letters, product authentication certificates for luxury timepieces, inventory insurance policy, e-commerce platform settlement reports (Stripe/PayPal), and an internal AML policy naming a Tracfin declarant (désignation d'un déclarant) under Article L561-33 CMF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or initial initial funding sourced from crypto exchanges, crowdfunding, or a third-party unrelated account; the bank refuses the wire as unexplained funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the originator bank, the MT103 with proper purpose code 'APPORT CAPITAL', notarized subscription resolution, capital deposit certificate from the escrow bank or notaire, source-of-wealth statement for any crypto liquidation (exchange transaction history and tax ledger), and shareholder loan agreement if funds are advanced by a shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident manager without French identity card, residence permit or French bank history; bank flags inability to verify identity lawfully, especially for authorized signatories resident abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/EEA passport + national ID, criminal record extract of the country of residence, Apostille legalization and certified French translation, proof of foreign professional address, and a signed declaration of acceptance of French AML obligations. If the bank still refuses, invoke the droit au compte (Article L312-1 CMF): a formal refusal letter triggers assignment of a bank by Banque de France within 10 business days.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions into France are unrestricted inbound EUR transfers. The sole compliant routing is: (1) the shareholder wires via SWIFT MT103 from a verified bank account in their own name to the SARL's IBAN; (2) the field 70 of the MT103 must carry the purpose code 'S301' or 'APPORT CAPITAL' (or 'Apport en compte courant d'associé' for shareholder loans); (3) for capital increases exceeding EUR 15 million per transaction, the SARL must file a Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration within 20 days, including the French intermediary bank; (4) the beneficiary bank will apply enhanced due diligence on the originator bank; funds are credited only if the SARL's Kbis name matches the IBAN; (5) escrow rules for capital deposit apply if the SARL is not yet registered at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce: funds are blocked on a 'compte de dépôt' until issuance of the Certificate of Registration. Evidence to retain: signed share subscription resolutions, third-party bank reference, notarized certificate of deposit, RBE filing and the MT103 substantiating inflow path.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements may be executed through (1) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments to EU suppliers (max EUR 100,000 per transaction with instant SEPA; no limit on standard SCT), (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR payments (USD, CHF, JPY) via correspondent banks, (3) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for high-value watch and jewelry imports (irrevocable, confirmed) to protect prepayment risk, and (4) documentary collections (D/P, D/A) for recurring supplier flows. Add: remittance information must include the vendor's legal name, invoice number and country; EU Regulation 2015/847 requires full originator and beneficiary data; for goods imports subject to customs, the DPE (Déclaration d'Echange de Biens) must be filed within the 10th working day of the month following the transaction; Stripe and PayPal EUR settlements are cleared via Standard SEPA/SEPA Instant to the SARL's main account on a daily or T+1 basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Forward FX (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF) – fully permitted; executed under the Convention-Cadre FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement or bank's ISDA-style undocumented spot/forward annex; requires credit line or margin of 2-5% of notional for a SARL; appropriate for USD-denominated watch procurement from Swiss/US distributors.

Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD) – permissible for dealers and non-financial counterparties under EMIR (EU Regulation 648/2012); requires a signed ISDA Master Agreement plus Credit Support Annex (CSA) for collateral; used only for hedges of long-term commercial contracts exceeding 12 months; transaction reporting to a registered trade repository is mandatory within one business day.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) – legally permissible in France but commercially irrelevant for EUR pairs because the euro is fully convertible; NDFs may be used only for settlement against non-convertible or lightly traded currencies (e.g., XOF, MAD, INR, CNY offshore CNH) to hedge invoice exposures; settlement is in EUR by net difference, subject to the same FBF master agreement and Banque de France derivatives statistical reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting (AGOA) convening, approving the annual financial statements, deciding profit appropriation/retained earnings, and ratifying the gérant's management acts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders recorded in the Register of Members; minutes kept in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, unless extended by court order; no public registry filing of the minutes is required for a standard SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene within the statutory window allows any shareholder to petition the president of the Commercial Court for the appointment of a mandated agent to call the meeting; gérant incurs civil liability and may be removed for cause; no fixed administrative fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS): balance sheet, income statement, annexes, allocation of reported profit, and declaration for non-publication where eligible
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court) of the registered-office locality; RCS notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval of the annual accounts and, in all cases, within 7 months of fiscal year-end; extension available only by court order upon petition prior to expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine up to EUR 1,500 for natural persons and EUR 7,500 for legal entities (C. com. art. L.247-1); the president of the Commercial Court may order filing within a fixed period under a coercive periodic penalty payment (astreinte); gérant exposure to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) via form n°2065-SD and supporting schedules 2050 to 2058-G, including statutory annual accounts reconciliation, depreciation and provisions, and deductible items
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) through professional mandatory electronic filing (EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year, by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for an off-calendar fiscal year, by the second business day after the fourth month following fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of net tax due, increased to 40% in bad faith and 80% in fraudulent cases, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2% (CGI art. 1728); tax authority may reject deductions and assess reassessments on account of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration annuelle de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs) confirming the identity, shareholding percentage, and control of every beneficial owner in the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and the French Registry of Beneficial Owners (RBE) maintained by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of the last beneficial-owner declaration; if shareholding or control changes, an updated declaration must be filed within 30 days of the event instead of awaiting the annual confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil/criminal fine up to EUR 15,000 for natural persons and EUR 75,000 for legal entities for failure to file or false declaration; inability to obtain registry attestations; publication of the enforcement decision and possible director disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for a SARL if, at the close of the fiscal year, the company exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet over EUR 4,000,000; turnover net of tax over EUR 8,000,000; average permanent headcount over 50. Audit is also mandatory if any shareholder holding at least one-third of the capital demands one or where required by consolidation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / ANC Regulation 2016-07); voluntary or consolidated financial statements of listed groups may apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must file an annual confirmation with the RCS within 30 days after the anniversary of the latest beneficial-owner declaration. The confirmation attests the continued accuracy of existing beneficial owner data; any modification occurring during the year, including a change to shareholding percentages or control structure, must be filed as an updated declaration within 30 days of the event. The annual confirmation is a distinct filing from the yearly accounts deposit and carries the registrar's fee schedule.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés): required to evidence shareholdings, transfers, and pledges of SARL shares
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and resolutions (registre des procès-verbaux / registre de décisions d'associés)
Share transfer register (registre des mouvements de titres): required for chronological recording of every transfer of shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 900 per year for registered-office domiciliation or registered agent service in France (Paris/city-center or business-centre arrangement)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per certified statutory audit engagement for a fashion-jewelry/watches e-commerce SARL if audit thresholds are exceeded or audit is otherwise required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on the first €38,120 of annual taxable profit (qualifying SMEs with revenue ≤ €10,000,000); R&D tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible expenditures; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% (up to €400,000 of eligible costs); exemption on long-term participation gains (no gains if held ≥ 2 years) under the mère-fille regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward; annual utilization capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the remaining taxable income; 1-year carryback possible capped at €1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD ('Déclaration de résultats' / liasse fiscale) filed electronically on the impots.gouv.fr professional portal via EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) / TéléTVA (TDFC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year fiscal years, by 3 May of the following year (moved to the first following working day if 3 May is a non-working day).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit subject to the reduced 15% rate (up to €38,120 tranche) and the standard 25% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a French establishment must compute the French-source taxable base and enter the amount after treaty business-profits and PE allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal loss of the period and losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report net operating loss eligible for indefinite carryforward; losses may be used only against future French-source profits of the same enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Long-term capital gains and losses on the sale of jewelry inventory (and short-term ordinary gains).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory of a merchandising business is ordinary income; only assets classified as fixed assets qualify for long-term treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may claim the CIR only through a French permanent establishment carrying on eligible research activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed before credits, plus the social contribution (contribution sociale sur l'impôt sur les sociétés, 3.3%, if turnover and tax thresholds are exceeded), and quarterly instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalment schedule: four advance payments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December; balance due with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, profit and loss statement, depreciation schedule, provisions, and cash-flow tables forming the liasse fiscale.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must file with the annexes in compliance with the French chart of accounts (Plan Comptable Général); non-resident companies without a French PE file no annexes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 5% surcharge of the tax due, increased to 10% if not filed within 30 days of a formal notice, 40% for deliberate misconduct (manquement délibéré), 80% for tax fraud or abuse of law; late payment interest of 0.20% per month; possible automatic assessment if no return is filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571 (quarterly instalment notices) and Form 2572 (final balance settlement) via TéléTVA/EDI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December for instalments; balance with the 2065 return by 3 May for calendar-year entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Instalment base / Tax base of the preceding fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount of corporate income tax that will be split into four instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The instalment is calculated by reference to the tax on the French-source profit of the last closed fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and electronic payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must obtain a French tax identification number from the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères to file and pay.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or absent instalments: the same 5%/10% surcharge scheme and 0.20% monthly late interest apply to the unpaid instalment; an administrative penalty of 0.5% per month applies for deficient advance payments in cases of persistent default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends distributed by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder (art. 119 bis 2 CGI).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC / formulaire 5000) from its competent tax authority and submit it to the paying agent before the distribution, or claim a refund by filing a written réclamation with the French tax authorities (DRFIP) within the statutory window (by 31 December of the second year following the withholding). The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption permits a 0% rate where the EU parent holds directly at least 5% of the distributing company's capital and has held it for 24 months (art. 145/216 CGI). Treaty rates generally apply at 0%, 5% or 15% (e.g., France-USA DTA: 5% for direct shareholding of 10% or more, 15% for portfolio dividends) upon TRC proof of beneficial ownership and the absence of treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: no general withholding tax on arm's-length royalties paid by a French company to a non-resident business; interest paid to non-resident corporations is generally exempt from French withholding tax, except interest to individuals (30%) and to beneficiaries resident in non-cooperative States (ETNC) taxed at 75% unless a treaty grants relief. Treaty rates under France's network typically sit at 0%-10% for royalties and 0%-15% for interest depending on the DTA and beneficial-ownership conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French Local File and Master File documentation (dossier de prix de transfert) is legally mandatory where gross annual turnover or gross fixed assets reach €400,000,000 (art. L. 13 AA and L. 13 AB CGI). Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory where the consolidating group's annual consolidated revenue reaches €750,000,000. The current SARL, operating below the €400M threshold, is not obliged to file a full TP dossier but must retain contemporaneous arm's-length evidence as Art. 57 CGI empowers the tax administration to recharacterise and adjust any inter-company transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies an anti-abuse and substance-over-form framework instead of a formal ESR regime: (i) art. L. 64 LPF abuse-of-law doctrine (80% penalty); (ii) the ATAD-inspired general anti-abuse rule and OECD Principal Purpose Test introduced into French domestic law; (iii) the 'place of effective management' residence test (art. 209 CGI) and the 'screen company' case law. The SARL must evidence genuine economic substance in France - a local registered office, an employed management team, board decisions made in France, physical inventory or warehouse arrangements, and real commercial activity - to sustain treaty protection, VAT rules, and non-application of the abuse-of-law penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Concealment (Fraude fiscale)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring sales of luxury jewelry and high-value timepieces, invoicing through nominee e-commerce platforms, using undisclosed offshore merchant accounts, or destroying accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: up to €500,000 fine per count and 5 years' imprisonment (increased to €1,000,000 and 7 years for organized-gang fraud); compulsory publication of the condemnation; electronic and passport surveillance measures; automatic referral of the case to the financial prosecutor (PNF) for aggravated circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant can be criminally prosecuted as principal perpetrator; travel bans, passport withdrawal, and bank-account seizures are available under judicial control; the tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil for the fraud penalties and seek civil restitution against the manager for the whole evaded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Shell Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a Luxembourg, Dubai or Hong Kong intermediary with no personnel or commercial substance to strip French jewelry sales margins, combined with payments of fictitious service fees or inflated wholesale discounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. L. 64 LPF: 80% penalty on the recharacterized tax base plus monthly late interest; possible criminal referral for abuse of law aggravated by fraud; professional disqualification from commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or approve the abusive scheme incur personal liability for the 80% penalty and interest; the commercial court (tribunal de commerce) may ban the manager from managing a company for a period of years; imprisonment up to 5 years applies if the scheme is also characterized as fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a related Hong Kong or Swiss jewelry supplier at deliberately inflated prices, or failing to document the arm's-length nature of intercompany purchase and marketing arrangements under art. 57 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of the full profit to the French SARL; 40% penalty for deliberate non-filing (manquement délibéré) and 80% for abuse of law; interest at 0.20% per month; possible 10-year limitation extension for undisclosed foreign transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who executed the overbilling is liable to civil restitution for the evaded IS, social contributions on fringe benefits and, in flagrant cases, criminal fines and imprisonment for money laundering (art. 324-1 Code pénal: 5 years and €375,000).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using personal PayPal or Stripe accounts to channel corporate jewelry sales, failing to register as a VASP/merchant with the regulator, refusing to disclose beneficial ownership, or carrying out cash transactions above the legal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Monetary and Financial Code L. 561 et seq. violations and Code pénal art. 324-1: corporate fines up to €375,000, confiscation of jewelry, turnover and import bans; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel and Tracfin may block payment accounts and blacklist the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers face 5 years' imprisonment, a €375,000 fine, professional prohibition, freezing orders, and travel bans while under investigation; civil liability for all proceeds laundered through the corporate accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Declare Economic Substance and Non-Cooperative State Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming the benefit of treaty relief while paying royalties, interest or dividends into bank accounts located in non-cooperative states (ETNC) or to a related entity without genuine economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 238 A CGI: disallowance of deductions and 75% withholding on the payments, reclassification of the full sums as constructive dividends or profit distributions; administrative penalties up to 40-80%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability with the company; the director cannot rely on the corporate shield where the payment arrangement was deliberately designed; criminal prosecution for complicity in tax evasion exposes the director to a €1,000,000 fine and 7 years' imprisonment.
